audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Gwen levels 1, 2, 3 and 4-5 and marked both item stages even, the exact inverse of the whys.
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw poke plus grey-health regen beats a mist-less melee early; Snip Snip!'s %-max-HP magic and true centre only take over once Riftmaker or Nashor's lands. whys[0], whys[5] and whys[6] already said this.
audit.corrected: Dr. Mundo / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Gwen / Gwen.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns given anywhere, including for Maximum Dosage, which the page calls a panic button you should fight through.
audit.why: Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s at every rank, Heart Zapper 17/16.5/16/15.5/15, Blunt Force Trauma 9/8.25/7.5/6.75/6 and Infected Bonesaw 4s. A 120-second ultimate that never gets shorter means one baited R buys you two full minutes of a Mundo who cannot reset a fight - that is a plan, and the page did not have it.
audit.corrected: late, whys[6] and spikes[3].text now name the 120s R and the anti-heal window it opens.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heart Zapper (W) is absent from the whole page, and Blunt Force Trauma is never called an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Heart Zapper stores damage he takes and heals it back when it ends, so trading into an active W is how a Gwen loses a fight she was winning on paper - the answer is to snip after it expires, not during. Blunt Force Trauma carries the autoReset flag, so the attack wind-up rather than the cast is the moment to be inside the mist.
audit.corrected: mid and wants.foe[1] now name Heart Zapper's stored-damage heal; early names the Blunt Force Trauma reset as the tell.

edits.before: Level 1 belongs to Mundo and you have to respect it — you have no mist, no E dash, just a slow six-snip cone Q, while his Q cleaver throws percent-current-HP poke that his passive grey-health regen heals back. Don't walk into cleaver range to force a fight you can't win yet; sidestep the cleaver, farm with the tips of Snip Snip!, and accept some chip. By level 2-3 you have Q to poke and can hold E for safety, but his early bulk and self-heal mean this is still a farm phase, not a kill phase. The good news: every point of HP he stacks is future fuel for your percent-max-HP autos and Q.
edits.after: Level 1 belongs to Mundo and you have to respect it — you have no mist, no E dash, just a slow six-snip cone Q, while his Q cleaver throws percent-current-HP poke that his passive grey-health regen heals back. Do not walk into cleaver range; sidestep it, farm with the tips of Snip Snip!, and accept some chip. His step-up opens on a Blunt Force Trauma auto reset, so the wind-up is your cue to back off, not the cast. By 2-3 you can poke and hold E for safety, but this is still a farm phase. Every point of HP he stacks is future fuel for your percent-max-HP autos and Q.

edits.before: This is the turning point but it's a skill phase, not a free win yet — at 6, Needlework plus full Q-W-E lets you actually duel him. The play is to drop Hallowed Mist on yourself so his autos and E-empowered swing can't target you, then snip his oversized bar — the center line of Snip Snip! lands TRUE damage his armor and bonus HP can't reduce, and your damage heals you back. Use Skip 'n Slash to reposition and refund the dash off hitting him, then reset and re-snip; just remember his Q cleaver is a skillshot the mist won't dodge, so keep moving. Anti-heal here is non-negotiable so his Q self-heal and passive regen don't undo your trades.
edits.after: This is the turning point but it is a skill phase, not a free win — at 6, Needlework plus full Q-W-E lets you actually duel him. Drop Hallowed Mist on yourself so his autos and the Blunt Force Trauma reset cannot target you, then snip his oversized bar: the centre line of Snip Snip! lands TRUE damage his armour and bonus HP cannot reduce, and your damage heals you back. Never dump a trade into an active Heart Zapper — it stores what you deal and gives it back as health, so snip after it expires. Skip 'n Slash repositions and refunds off hitting him; his Q cleaver is a skillshot the mist will not dodge, so keep moving.

edits.before: This is your kingdom and the rare lane where late game gets BETTER for you, not worse. Unlike most scalers, Mundo doesn't out-scale you — he just stacks the exact stat you punish: HP. Your percent-max-HP magic and the true-damage center line of Snip Snip! ignore all the armor and bonus health he buys, so the fatter he gets the harder you cut. His R Maximum Dosage is a massive instant heal plus regen, so keep anti-heal up and force the fight inside Hallowed Mist where his autos can't reach you and you can grind through the heal. Don't disengage off his R panic-button — commit, snip, and out-DPS the regen.
edits.after: This is your kingdom and the rare lane where late game gets BETTER for you. Mundo does not out-scale you — he stacks the exact stat you punish: HP. Your percent-max-HP magic and the true-damage centre line of Snip Snip! ignore all the armour and bonus health he buys, so the fatter he gets the harder you cut. Maximum Dosage is a huge instant heal plus regen on a flat 120s at every rank, so keep Grievous Wounds up, bait it once, and the next two minutes are a Mundo who cannot reset a fight. Do not disengage off his R — commit, snip, and out-DPS the regen inside the mist.

edits.before: The more tank items and HP he buys the harder your percent-max-HP and true damage cut, and anti-heal answers Maximum Dosage — you shred this drain-tank inside the mist.
edits.after: The more tank items and HP he buys the harder your percent-max-HP and true damage cut, and Grievous Wounds answers a 120s Maximum Dosage — you shred this drain-tank inside the mist.

edits.before: Riftmaker/Nashor's is your takeover — Snip Snip!'s percent-max-HP magic and Thousand Cuts on-hit ignore the armor he builds, and the more HP he stacks the harder you cut, so out-DPS his Q self-heal here.
edits.after: Riftmaker/Nashor's is your takeover — Snip Snip!'s percent-max-HP magic and A Thousand Cuts on-hit ignore the armour he builds, and the more HP he stacks the harder you cut, so out-DPS his Q self-heal here.

edits.before: Mundo's R Maximum Dosage gives a huge instant heal plus regen, MS and AD — but your percent-max-HP magic, true-damage center snips and anti-heal out-shred his heal-per-second, so commit inside Hallowed Mist and grind him down instead of letting him run.
edits.after: Maximum Dosage is a huge instant heal plus regen, MS and AD on a flat 120s at every rank — but percent-max-HP magic, true-damage centre snips and Grievous Wounds out-shred his heal-per-second, so bait it, then commit inside Hallowed Mist and grind him down.

edits.before: Buy anti-heal (Sorcerer's/anti-heal item) early so his passive grey-health regen, Q self-heal and R Maximum Dosage can't out-sustain your DPS
edits.after: Buy Grievous Wounds early so his grey-health regen, Q self-heal, stored Heart Zapper damage and Maximum Dosage cannot out-sustain your DPS

edits.after: Stack HP and soak your burst in Heart Zapper to heal it back, until Maximum Dosage and grey-health regen out-heal you

notes: The prose is good and already second-person; the chart was inverted against it. win[] and phases[].side gave Gwen levels 1 through 4-5 and called the item stages even, while whys[0] says Mundo owns level 1 and whys[5] and whys[6] say the item stages are Gwen's takeover. Corrected to Dr. Mundo/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Gwen/Gwen, which is also what the 55.96% win rate over 831 games looks like: a losing start that becomes a strong scaling win. Two abilities were missing entirely. Heart Zapper (W, 17s at rank 1) is never named anywhere despite being the ability that decides whether his trade heals him. Blunt Force Trauma (E) is described as an 'E-empowered swing' but never identified as an auto-attack reset, which is the actual tell. 'Thousand Cuts' was missing its 'A'.
